output: Hypothesis: There is no statistically significant relationship between time preference factors (such as DISSAVED and SAMESAVE) and BMI in the 1989 data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79). The observed relationships between these variables and BMI are weak and not statistically significant, as indicated by the low correlation values and the lack of p-values for the regression coefficients. This suggests that time preference factors may not be a major determinant of BMI in this dataset.
